extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: A dataset of 7,787 natural, grade-school science questions partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions), designed to encourage AI research in advanced question answering requiring reasoning and knowledge beyond simple retrieval methods.
extraction.creator: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were drawn from a variety of sources through extensive search and investigation over several months. The dataset consists of natural science questions authored for standardized tests, targeting grade levels from 3rd to 9th grade.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Natural science questions authored for standardized tests, drawn from various sources including a subset of the 2016 Allen AI Science Challenge questions and other public-domain test sources.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The ARC dataset was partitioned into a Challenge Set (2590 questions) and an Easy Set (5197 questions). Challenge questions were operationally defined as those answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm (IR solver) and a word co-occurrence algorithm (PMI solver). The IR solver searches for explicit statements of question+answer in a corpus using Elasticsearch, returning the top retrieved sentence with non-stopword overlap with both question and answer. The PMI solver measures associational strength between question and answer n-grams using pointwise mutual information calculated from corpus co-occurrence within a 10-word window. Questions correctly answered by either algorithm were placed in the Easy Set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set based on whether they were answered incorrectly by both an IR (Information Retrieval) solver and a PMI (Pointwise Mutual Information) solver. Challenge questions are those that both baseline solvers failed to answer correctly.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were originally authored by human examiners for standardized tests with grade-level assignments. The correct answers were provided as part of the original test materials.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Information Retrieval (IR) solver using Elasticsearch and Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) solver were used to partition questions into Challenge and Easy sets.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Questions target student grade levels from 3rd to 9th grade (ages 8-13 years).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset exhibits a retrieval bias in the Challenge Set by design - questions were specifically filtered to exclude those answerable by simple retrieval or word co-occurrence methods. This creates a bias towards questions requiring more complex reasoning. The underlying baseline methods show a retrieval bias towards sentences very similar to the question, and away from sentences that individually only partially match but together could explain the answer through chaining or multi-hop reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set definition is based on failure of two specific baseline algorithms (IR and PMI), which only approximates the informal goal of identifying 'hard' questions. The dataset contains only non-diagram, multiple-choice questions, excluding questions requiring visual reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is partitioned into train/dev/test sets for training and evaluating question-answering systems. Challenge Set is designed for testing advanced reasoning capabilities. Easy Set provides baseline comparison. The dataset is intended to encourage AI research in advanced question answering requiring reasoning and knowledge beyond simple retrieval methods.
